national_raw_news.title: 6 hours ago | National 165 India calls on BRICS countries to expand opportunities for women-led enterprises in global trade
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal has called on BRICS countries to work together to expand opportunities for women entrepreneurs and women-led enterprises in international trade. Addressing the BRICS WBA Women-Led Development Conference in New Delhi yesterday, Mr Goyal stressed the need for easier access to credit and markets, along with predictable business rules. The Commerce Minister said India is focused on empowering women through financial inclusion, education, skills and improved quality of life, with the aim of making them drivers of the country’s growth. He noted that nearly 300 million women in India have bank accounts, while collateral-free loans are provided to women seeking to start their own work, including those without a credit history. Mr Goyal also said around 100 million rural women are members of over nine million self-help groups under the ‘Lakhpati Didis’ initiative, aimed at ensuring women’s economic independence and greater contribution to India’s growth. Mr Goyal also urged governments to encourage women-owned enterprises to participate more actively in international expositions, conferences, seminars, exhibitions and business forums. Calling for greater engagement among BRICS countries, the minister said dialogue and diplomacy are the way forward towards a more prosperous future for member countries, partner countries and the world. He also highlighted that India has set a target of growing from a four trillion dollar economy today to a thirty trillion dollar economy by 2047, when the country celebrates 100 years of Independence.

national_raw_news.title: 6 hours ago | National 178 India ramps up Nepal flood relief with 8th aid flight, specialised tunnel team and forensic experts
national_raw_news.content: India has intensified its humanitarian assistance to Nepal in the wake of devastating flash floods, delivering over 130 tonnes of relief material and deploying 54 expert personnel to support search, rescue, and forensic operations. The Indian Embassy in Nepal said yesterday that an eighth Indian Air Force aircraft carrying 35 tonnes of relief and rescue supplies landed in Kathmandu, marking the latest shipment in a continuous aid effort launched on August 26, 2026. India has also dispatched specialised technical gear, including mud rescue suits, gas detectors, breathing apparatus, inflatable walkways, portable generators, lighting towers, and dewatering pumps. India has provided DNA kits, reagents, and equipment for DNA profiling to aid in victim identification. Earlier, the Ministry of External Affairs also noted the handing over of the relief aid by Indian Ambassador Naveen Srivastava to Nepal’s Minister Mahabir Pun upon the arrival of the eighth aircraft. Meanwhile, India’s specialised tunnel rescue team initially launched joint operations with the Nepali Army across two high-risk sites in Chilime and Langtang. Search efforts are currently concentrated at the Chilime tunnel, where rescue workers face severe operational hurdles due to rugged terrain, constrained access, and steep tunnel inclines. Teams are currently constructing a makeshift access path to transport heavy machinery, such as excavators, directly to the tunnel entrance. Construction on the track is progressing steadily and is expected to be completed within two to three days.

national_raw_news.title: Mizoram CM calls for strengthening Irrigation & Water Resources Department 3 hours ago 38
national_raw_news.content: Mizoram Chief Minister Lalduhoma has called for strengthening the Irrigation and Water Resources Department (IWRD), citing its expanding responsibilities and persistent shortage of manpower and technical expertise, official sources said. Lalduhoma made the remarks yesterday while chairing a meeting at the to review measures to strengthen the department. IWRD Minister PC Vanlalruata and senior officials from the General Administration Department, DP&AR, Finance Department and IWRD attended the meeting. The Chief Minister said several departments had been functioning with inadequate manpower for years and could weaken further because of staff shortages. He said the IWRD had remained in virtually the same position for the past 19 years despite a significant expansion in its activities and responsibilities. The department, earlier known as the Minor Irrigation department, is now involved in irrigation development as well as river basin planning, springshed development, integrated water resources management, hydrological data management, flood management and warning systems, multipurpose reservoirs and groundwater development, he said. During the meeting, IWRD chief engineer K Hamleta presented proposals for strengthening the department and briefed the meeting on the proposed follow-up measures, the sources said. The discussions focused on addressing the department’s manpower and technical requirements in view of its expanding role, it said.
